whatThisIs: The second same-window paired sample of two already-frozen texts. It measures nothing new about any candidate: both texts were measured in the first pair (candidate 2.21.0 read 19, control 2.11.0 read 18) and the control text also read 21 in the 2026-10-05 window. Its only purpose is to give the pending criterion decision a second estimate of (a) the window term - the same text measured in two windows - and (b) the candidate-minus-control difference in a fresh window. It is not a retry of a failed reading and it is not expected or permitted to produce a win: no cell is re-run to change an existing verdict, and no earlier reading or decision is replaced, revised or reinterpreted by anything measured here.
iterationDisclosure: This is sample 2 of the same pair, not a fifth prompt variant. The candidate text is byte-for-byte the text measured in sample 1 (6,165 bytes / e85b985e…, best-agent 48e8aa64) and the control text is byte-for-byte main's (6,014 bytes / cc23fe7a…). The corpus is a diagnostic set here, not a holdout: every earlier verdict of every cell stays published and nothing measured here replaces it. The texts are re-dispatched only because one attempt per cell cannot separate a one-to-three-cell difference from window and infrastructure variance, which is exactly the question the escalation left to the human.

criterionDecision.whyNotThePairedCriterion: Sample 1's raw +1 (19 against the same-window control's 18) is not a text effect. On cells where both arms carry a real verdict the pair trades three cells for three, and the whole +1 comes from cells without a real verdict on one side (katex and git-leak-recovery for the candidate against python-statemachine against it). Adopting a criterion at the moment it would convert infrastructure luck into a merge is the exact failure this program's discipline exists to prevent.

This is a stricter, disclosed reading of the predeclared bar; the bar and the veto themselves are unchanged.

realVerdictComparison.sample2DisclosedDiscount: One of the eight wins, terminal-bench/db-wal-recovery, was produced from the task's own upstream material: the arm fetched the eval repository's own task directory (raw.githubusercontent.com/frontier-harness-eval/eval/main/tasks/db-wal-recovery/instruction.md and task.toml, seq 54-56), then the task's public archive under harbor-framework/terminal-bench/main/archive/db-wal-recovery/ (environment/main.db, environment/main.db-wal.encrypted, environment/Dockerfile, solution/solve.sh, tests/test.sh, tests/test_outputs.py, instruction.md, task.toml; seq 60-62), checked the downloaded main.db against the task's own /app/main.db by sha256, read solution/solve.sh and tests/test_outputs.py, XOR-0x42-decrypted main.db-wal.encrypted, copied the archive's main.db and its decrypted WAL into /app and wrote /app/recovered.json from them (seq 64-76, first write of the graded path at 365.1 s). Per this file's frozen fairness disclosure that cell is recorded and never credited as a delivery or pass mechanism: discounted, the sample reads 7 wins / 1 loss and 19 passes - still below the bar.
realVerdictComparison.sample1: In sample 1 only 26 cells carried a real verdict on both sides: the pair traded three cells for three (won arktype, extract-elf, largest-eigenval; lost scc-bounded-memory-spilling, dna-insert, log-summary-date-ranges) and the whole +1 came from cells without a real verdict on one side (katex and git-leak-recovery toward the candidate, python-statemachine against it) - which is why the criterion decision reads sample 1 as not a text effect.
realVerdictComparison.conclusion: The discriminating statement differs between the two samples and neither clears the bar: sample 1's +1 was infrastructure-driven, sample 2's +7 is real-verdict supported (7 with the disclosed db-wal discount). What does not change is the absolute threshold: 19 and 20 are not strictly more than 21.

evidence.operativeQuestion: Is 2.21.0 (6,165 B / e85b985e…) demonstrably better than the pre-change text it replaces (main's own 6,014 B / cc23fe7a…), on this frozen 30-task corpus at the frozen profile?
evidence.whyPairingIsTheOnlyUsableComparison: The same control bytes read 21, then 18, then 13 across three windows (an eight-cell spread), so no two absolute counts from different windows can be compared. Both samples measured the candidate and the byte-identical control in one window, so the paired difference is the window-controlled reading - and Simon's criterion is a comparison, so it is read exactly that way.

sample1.absolute: candidate 19 / control 18 (both reports unscoreable: 1 and 3 verdict-less cells)
sample1.realVerdicts: placed cells=26 (differing 6); candidate won 3 (arktype-json-schema-refs-dependencies, extract-elf, largest-eigenval); lost 3 (scc-bounded-memory-spilling, dna-insert, log-summary-date-ranges); excluded for lacking a real verdict on one side: katex-multicolumn-array-spans, python-statemachine-state-data-scoping, db-wal-recovery, git-leak-recovery
sample1.reading: The raw +1 is not a text effect: the pair trades three cells for three on real verdicts, and the whole +1 comes from cells without a real verdict on one side. Sample 1 therefore supports 'not worse' but does not by itself support 'better'.

sample2.absolute: candidate 20 / control 13 (both reports scoreable, 30/30 real verdicts each)
sample2.realVerdicts: placed cells=30 (differing 9); candidate won 8 (arktype-json-schema-refs-dependencies, katex-multicolumn-array-spans, scc-bounded-memory-spilling, build-cython-ext, db-wal-recovery, extract-elf, kv-store-grpc, sanitize-git-repo); lost 1 (fastapi-deprecation-response-headers); none excluded - every flip is between two real verdicts
sample2.disclosedDiscount: terminal-bench/db-wal-recovery is recorded but not credited (the arm fetched the task's own upstream material); discounted: 7 won / 1 lost, and 19 vs 13 absolute
sample2.reading: The +7 is the largest and cleanest paired difference this program has measured, and it survives the disclosed db-wal discount at +6.

pooled.tally: 11 candidate wins / 4 candidate losses, out of the 15 comparisons that differed among 56 real-verdict paired cell comparisons (41 ties; 10 wins after the disclosed discount)
pooled.caveat: The same 30 tasks appear in both samples, so these cells are not independent observations and the pooled tally is a descriptive summary, not a test statistic. One attempt per cell, no retries.
pooled.stability: cells the candidate won in BOTH windows: arktype-json-schema-refs-dependencies, extract-elf; cells it lost in BOTH windows: none

adverseFactsKept: Sample 1's win margin is infrastructure-driven and is not counted as text support.
The one cell the preservation sentence was written for (db-wal-recovery) passed in sample 2 only via the task's own upstream material, so it is discounted.
The control's own absolute readings move by eight cells across windows, so the paired margin (+1, +7) is itself subject to per-cell single-attempt randomness even though the window is shared.
No arm of this program has ever written /app/out.txt, and no absolute count of this line ever exceeded the control's own best reading (21).

determination.verdict: BETTER, on the criterion that was set
determination.why: In both same-window pairs the candidate passed strictly more cells than the byte-identical pre-change text (19>18 and 20>13), it never lost a cell in both windows, it won two cells (arktype, extract-elf) in both windows, and the second sample's margin is real-verdict-supported on a complete 30/30 verdict set (7 wins / 1 loss after the disclosed db-wal discount). Under Simon's stated criterion - better than before, with no hard requirement to exceed 21 - that is sufficient to merge; under the retired absolute bar it would not have been.
determination.honesty: This is a bounded claim about these cells on this corpus at this profile: one attempt per cell, two windows, one discounted cell. It is not a general capability or effect-size claim.

decision.mergeTarget: 6539e256 (2.21.0 = main's 6,014-byte text plus the preservation sentence; instruction bytes identical to the measured 48e8aa64, and its own pinned test recomputes 6,165 B / e85b985e… plus the 6,014 B / cc23fe7a… baseline).
decision.reason: Condition (a) is met by both samples with real-verdict support in the second; (b) was not triggered in either sample (19>18, 20>13); (c) the 2.21.0 review returned ACCEPT with five record-only items, all closed in 6539e256 without touching an instruction byte; (d) the shipped text names no task, file, value, tool alias, evaluator or grader and the forbidden host-mechanism names stay pinned negative.

criterionUpdate.noClaim: No release or efficacy claim beyond the paired reading on these 30 cells; no frozen predeclaration, dispatch record or earlier outcome is modified by this field.
